info.desc: Born in the U.S.A. is the seventh studio album by rock singer-songwriter Bruce Springsteen, released on June 4, 1984. Often considered his most popular and commercial triumph, it saw Springsteen (in contrast to his previous album, the critical favorite Nebraska) experimenting with anthemic arrangements and a 1980s production incorporating a radio-friendly sound that was embraced warmly by both critics and the audience. Springsteen also delivered a new look to his public – he was reintroduced as a tougher and muscular rock star after two years of running and bodybuilding. These efforts and innovative strategies resulted in Springsteen's peak of commercial .

podcast.body: Released on June 4, 1984, this album features a cover photo of Bruce's backside in well-worn jeans, with a cap sticking out of his pocket and the American flag in the background, signaling a different, less solemn sound than its predecessor, "Nebraska." The song's verses tell a poignant story of a young man from a hometown jam being sent to war, killing "the yellow man," and returning home to unemployment and a dismissive VA, detailing a betrayal of American veterans rather than a patriotic anthem. It reached number nine on the Billboard Hot 100 in the fall of 1984 and was named number 59 out of the top 365 songs of the 20th century by the Recording Industry Association of America. "Born in the USA made it to number nine on the billboard hot 100 in the fall of 1984 the recording industry association of America named it number 59 out of the top 365 songs of the 20th century."

podcast.body: The album launched a run of hits in 1984, with three of its tracks reaching the top ten on the charts that year. "His run of Born in the USA hits was just starting in 84. Dancing in the dark, cover me, and the title track from his album were top ten's that year. That's just three."

podcast.body: This album was a "stellar" nominee for Album of the Year at the 1985 Grammy Awards, which recognized music from 1984 and late 1983. It ultimately lost to Lionel Richie's "Can't Slow Down." "among the stellar album of the year nominees were, Prince's Purple Rain, Cindy Loppers She's So Unusual, Bruce Springsteen's Born in the USA, and Tina Turner's Private Dancer."
